70: If he can push matters off [with a justifiable excuse] - And say for this purpose I entered, he will feel secure and will not be afraid {to touch the wine}, for when he entered the house he entered with the  intention of libation, and thinks [to himself] if they find me I can push them off. Even though with regard to touching the wine he has no justifiable reason, [nevertheless the wine] is forbidden, for if he did not intend to make a libation why did he enter? We cannot compare this to the {earlier} case of leaving a gentile in one's shop {and the wine is not forbidden}, because there the gentile entered with permission {presumably to buy wine} and we know why he entered  [the shop], so as long as the owner does not inform him he is leaving [the wine is permitted] as he [the gentile] thinks to himself if I touch the wine now [the owner] will come in and see. {Rashi  makes a very suttle difference between the two cases. In both cases the gentile is allowed to be there. The suttle difference is in the case of the shop we know exactly why he is in the shop, in the case of our Gemoroh, although he can give a valid reason why he entered, but we do not know for what purpose he entered and the default assumption is, his intention is to make wine libations}.
And if - he cannot push off [has no justifiable reason why he is there], and since he is anxious [for even] entering, he is afraid and will not [go on to] touch.
The innkeeper locked the door - And the gentile was secluded with the wine, or the Jew said to the gentile guard [meaning] stand outside and guard.

It is forbidden - We are concerned that perhaps he went up [in], since he [the Jew] told him [the gentile] 'guard' he [the gentile] feels secure that he [the Jew] has separated [distanced] himself from him.
